newsitem.title: USA: U S West sells 4.4 mln Time Warner shares.
newsitem.headline: U S West sells 4.4 mln Time Warner shares.

text.p: U S West Media Group has sold its stake in Time Warner Inc to Salomon Brothers Inc for about $220 million, U S West said Thursday.

It said the sale of the 4.4 million shares -- about 0.7 percent of Time Warner's outstanding shares -- is part of a plan to liquidate nonstrategic assets and is not related to U S West's 25 percent stake in Time Warner Entertainment.
U S West and Time Warner have been in protracted negotiations over the structure of their Time Warner Entertainment partnership, which owns Warner Bros, HBO and most of Time Warner's cable systems.

"There is a chronological relationship between this and the other coverage of our negotiations (over the Time Warner Entertainment partnership), but just because of that coincidence it doesn't mean there's a cause and effect relationship -- and there isn't," U S West Media spokesman Steve Lang said in an interview.
"That was just some odds-and-ends stock left over from when U S West Media bought Continental," said Tom Wolzien, an analyst with Sanford C. Bernstein.

U S West inherited the holdings when it bought Continental Cablevision -- renamed Media One -- for $11.8 billion in November 1996. The shares were left over from a move in 1987 by members of the cable industry to bail out Ted Turner's struggling cable operations.
U S West earlier this year announced a plan to shed about $1 billion in nonstrategic holdings, Lang said. To date, it has sold or has agreements to sell about $700 million of those holdings.
